summary: Sporting News covers the 23-man USMNT roster Gregg Berhalter announced on October 5, 2023 for friendlies against Germany (October 14, Hartford) and Ghana (October 17, Nashville). Key storylines are Gio Reyna's first call-up under Berhalter since the 2022 World Cup falling out, Julian Nagelsmann's debut as Germany coach, and injury absences including captain Tyler Adams and Antonee Robinson.
one_line: Gregg Berhalter named a 23-man USMNT roster for October 2023 friendlies against Germany and Ghana, featuring Gio Reyna's return and several injury absences.
key_facts: The USMNT plays Germany in Hartford, Connecticut on October 14, 2023, and Ghana at GEODIS Park in Nashville, Tennessee on October 17.
The match against Germany is the debut for new German head coach Julian Nagelsmann, 36, who has been out of work since leaving Bayern Munich in March.
Germany, ranked 15th, qualifies automatically for Euro 2024 as host, which opens its schedule for friendlies.
The USA and Ghana have a history of contentious matchups, including three consecutive World Cups in 2006, 2010, and 2014.
The roster was announced Thursday, October 5, and has 23 players, one fewer than the September friendlies against Uzbekistan and Oman.
PSV midfielder Malik Tillman withdrew due to injury and Alex Zendejas of Club America was named in his place.
Captain Tyler Adams remains out with a long-term hamstring injury; he was hurt at Leeds United in March and played just 20 minutes on his Bournemouth debut in the EFL Cup before a setback.
Antonee Robinson is absent with a sports hernia; Zack Steffen, Sean Johnson, Josh Sargent (ankle) and Daryl Dike (torn Achilles) are also out.
Christian Pulisic of AC Milan leads the roster with 62 caps and 26 goals; Weston McKennie has 46 caps and 11 goals.
Lennard Maloney, a 23-year-old Heidenheim midfielder born in Berlin to an American father, received his first call-up with 0 caps.
Gio Reyna, 20, returns from a leg fracture and is called in by Berhalter for the first time since their falling out at the 2022 World Cup.
Reyna's parents' actions after the World Cup sparked a domestic violence investigation of Berhalter before his re-hire; Berhalter said they spoke 'weeks ago' on Zoom.
Berhalter sees Reyna playing central midfielder, attacking midfielder, or winger in a 'between the lines' style, and wants to 'get him minutes' since Reyna has not played for his club this season.
Johnny Cardoso, who missed September camp with an ankle injury, is included after returning to action with Brazilian club Internacional.
